stem: In triangle \(XYZ\), \(XY = XZ\) and the measure of angle \(Y\) is \(52^{\circ}\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(X\)?
solution: Because \(XY = XZ\), the angles opposite these sides, \(Z\) and \(Y\), are equal, so angle \(Z\) also measures \(52^{\circ}\).
The angles of a triangle add up to \(180^{\circ}\): \(180 - 52 - 52 = 76\).
verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert abs(d('X','Y')-d('X','Z'))<0.01 and abs(ang('X','Y','Z')-52)<0.1
ans=180-2*52
assert abs(ang('Y','X','Z')-ans)<0.1
assert Rational(spr_answers[0])==ans==76
